This is verifiable, in-diff, and decision-relevant: any out-of-tree consumer parsing the old array format breaks on deploy. The in-tree callers were updated in lockstep so it is not an in-tree defect, making it a concrete compatibility/architecture risk for a maintainer to weigh rather than a verifiable bug in this codebase.

judged_text: The public /groups/:name/members response changed from a bare serialized array to {members: [...], meta: {...}} and the default limit dropped from unbounded (200 for automatic groups) to 50, with no compatibility or versioning path. Any plugin, theme, or API consumer that parses the old array response or relied on receiving all members breaks silently when this deploys — in-tree callers were updated in lockstep but out-of-tree consumers receive an object where they expect an array.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a deliberate breaking change to the public `GroupsController#members` endpoint: it previously did `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (bare array response), but now always returns an object `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` and always paginates with `limit = (params[:limit] || 50)` (previously non-automatic groups were unbounded and automatic groups defaulted to 200). In-tree Ember callers were updated to use `result.members`/`result.meta` (e.g., `Discourse.Group#findMembers`), but the diff provides no compatibility/versioning shim for out-of-tree consumers. This is a real, diff-grounded review concern about API compatibility, not an internal correctness defect by itself.
